issues.legal_issue: A tenant's deposit of the full rent arrears, interest, and assessed costs with the Rent Controller before the first hearing satisfies the statutory payment requirement when the deposit remains available to the landlord and the landlord is informed of it at the first hearing.
material_facts: A landlord filed an application to evict a tenant for non-payment of rent.
Before the first hearing, the tenant deposited the rent arrears, calculated at the fair rent fixed by the Rent Controller, with that Controller.
The deposit included the required interest and costs and remained with the Controller on the first hearing date.
At the first hearing, the Controller informed the landlord's counsel that the amount had been deposited and was available to the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The tenant fulfilled the statutory payment requirement and was protected from eviction on the ground of rent default; the landlord's eviction application had to be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to section 13(2)(i) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, payment or tender of the arrears, interest, and costs by the first hearing deems the rent to have been paid within the required time. A deposit made before the hearing counts as a deposit on the hearing date if it remains in court and is available to the landlord, who is informed of it. The Court distinguished Vidya Prachar Trust v. Basant Ram because that case involved a partial tender and a deposit in a different court under unrelated proceedings, and followed Duli Chand v. Maman Chand. It overruled Mehnga Singh v. Dewan Dilbagh Rai.

predicates.rent_default_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant for non-payment of rent.
predicates.tenant_deposited_full_arrears_before_fir: The tenant deposited the full rent arrears with the court handling the eviction proceeding before its first hearing.
predicates.deposit_included_required_interest_and_c: The tenant's deposit included the interest and costs required for the rent-default proceeding.
predicates.deposit_remained_available_at_first_hear: The deposited money remained with the court and could be paid to the landlord at the first hearing.
predicates.landlord_was_informed_of_deposit: The court informed the landlord or the landlord's representative at the first hearing that the deposit had been made.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a rent-default eviction proceeding deposits the full arrears, required interest, and costs before the first hearing, and the money remains available to the landlord who is informed of it, the tenant is protected from eviction for rent default.

issues.legal_issue: A deposit of rent with the court handling the landlord's eviction proceeding is a permissible form of payment when the deposit is available to the landlord without hindrance and the landlord knows of it.
material_facts: The tenant deposited the rent arrears with the Rent Controller who was handling the landlord's eviction application.
The deposit remained in the Controller's custody and the landlord could withdraw it.
The Controller informed the landlord's counsel of the deposit on the first hearing date.
issues.conclusion: The deposit with the Rent Controller was a valid mode of payment under the statutory proviso.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(2)(i) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, uses the alternatives of paying or tendering and does not prescribe a particular method of deposit. A tenant may tender payment to the landlord or deposit it in the court handling the eviction case, provided the deposit is available to the landlord without hindrance and the landlord knows of it. The Court distinguished Vidya Prachar Trust v. Basant Ram, where the deposit was made in a different court in unrelated proceedings and was not available to the landlord in the same way, and followed Duli Chand v. Maman Chand.

issues.definition: A deposit made in the court handling a rent-default eviction proceeding is a valid mode of payment when the landlord knows of it and can obtain the money without hindrance.
